title: Reliability enablement sprint kickoff & runbook inventory
content:
Purpose
This doc is a working kickoff brief for the cross-functional Reliability Enablement Sprint (working name: "Signal Stabilize Sprint"). Goal is to produce a prioritized, tested SLO baseline for 3 pilot services, an ownerable runbook inventory, and a communication/rollback pattern that product + infra teams can adopt. This is intentionally light on process — we want a pragmatic 4-week run to de-risk SLO adoption and clarify operational ownership.

Context & motivation
- Multiple product teams have asked for clearer SLO targets and an 'oncall-ready' runbook set.
- We need to standardize how we derive SLO targets from customer impact, not just historical p99 latency.
- This sprint will create artifacts that feed the broader Reliability Program: SLO templates, measurement dashboards, and a co-owned incident escalation ladder.

Scope (what we will deliver in 4 weeks)
1) SLO baseline documents for three pilot services (Search API, Chat Ingress, Embedding ingestion): target, measurement window, error budget policy, and rollback trigger points.
2) Runbook inventory and prioritized gap list for each pilot (runbook exists / needs update / missing).
3) Minimal dashboards for SLO signal (SLO burn rate, latency distribution, error-class breakdown).
4) Communication & escalation protocol for SLO breaches (pager escalation chain, Slack templates, postmortem owner mapping).
5) Lightweight automation: one alert -> link to relevant runbook & quick rollback play.

Success criteria (how we judge this sprint)
- Each pilot has an SLO doc accepted by product + SRE (sign-off by product manager and SRE lead).
- Runbook coverage >= 80% for oncall-critical paths for each pilot (manual check).
- Alerts route to the correct oncall rotation with an actionable runbook link < 2 minutes.
- One can demonstrate a simulated breach and execute a rollback/play in < 20 minutes during a tabletop.

Key stakeholders & roles
- Program lead (facilitation): Lena Thompson
- SRE engineering partner: Ravi Menon
- Product owners: Emily Zhao (Search), Tomás Ortega (Embeddings), Marcus Nguyen (Chat)
- Observability: Platform observability team (owner: Priya Shah)
- Release engineering: review rollback automation (owner: Omar Castillo)
- Solutions/SE: customer impact validation (owner: Amrita Singh)
- Legal/security: consult for private deployments if needed (owner: Naomi Reid)

Working assumptions / constraints
- Pilot services are hosted in Redwood Dedicated and Hosted; metrics plumbing exists for p50/p95/p99 and error counts, but SLI definitions will need refinement.
- We will not change long-term capacity or architecture in this sprint; focus is measurement, playbooks, and owners.
- No SLA commitments made externally from sprint outcomes.

Timeline (4-week cadence)
Week 0 (pre-kickoff): align stakeholders, gather current runbooks and metric dashboards (owners copy artifacts into sprint folder).
Week 1: SLI definition workshop + initial SLO target proposals. Runbook triage across pilots.
Week 2: Implement measurement queries + create dashboards; remediate top 3 runbook gaps.
Week 3: Tabletop exercises (simulate breaches), finalize alert -> runbook mapping, and finalize escalation chain.
Week 4: Sign-offs, handoff to Ops, and retrospective with action backlog.

Sprint rituals & communication
- Twice-weekly sync (Mon/Wed 30 min) — quick blockers, ownership updates.
- SLO design office hours (drop-in) — Thu afternoons for product teams to consult.
- Daily async updates in Slack thread: #reliability-program with topic tags (e.g., [SLO][Search]).
- Central artifact directory: Confluence page linked above + folder in Drive (add artifacts to the sprint folder).

Decision criteria for SLOs (practical heuristic)
1) Customer impact first: map observable symptoms to user-visible degradation (e.g., 5xx rate on Search -> query failures).
2) Choose SLI that correlates to user experience (success rate, end-to-end latency bucket, or degradation events).
3) Start conservative: pick a target that reflects current performance + reasonable improvement (avoid unrealistic jumps).
4) Use burn-rate-based short-term alerts to protect error budgets rather than static thresholds.

Top risks & mitigations
- Risk: Teams disagree on SLO targets. Mitigation: Run a 48-hour A/B measurement window with impact annotations and use SRE tie-break decision if no consensus.
- Risk: Missing metric fidelity for some SLIs. Mitigation: fall back to proxy SLIs (e.g., error counts by route) and log a technical debt ticket for measurement improvements.
- Risk: Runbooks are outdated. Mitigation: assign a runbook sprint task owner and require a second reviewer sign-off during Week 2.

Deliverable checklist (owner + status placeholders)
- SLO doc: Search API (owner: Emily Zhao) — DRAFT
- SLO doc: Chat Ingress (owner: Marcus Nguyen) — DRAFT
- SLO doc: Embedding Ingest (owner: Tomás Ortega) — DRAFT
- Runbook inventory spreadsheet (owner: Ravi Menon) — IN PROGRESS
- Dashboards: Search / Chat / Embedding (owner: Priya Shah) — TODO
- Tabletop script & scenario list (owner: Lena Thompson) — TODO

Tabletop exercise outline (30-45m per pilot)
1) Brief scenario and expected SLI behavior (5m)
2) Trigger alert, validate runbook linkage (5m)
3) Execute rollback or stabilization play (10-15m)
4) Post-exercise notes: what was missing, what was confusing, what needs automation (10m)

Notes to self / open questions (working)
- How strict should default error budgets be for internal services (vs customer-facing)?
- Do we want a templated message that product PMs push to customers when an SLO breach affects them?
- Can release-engineering provide a one-click rollback artifact linking to the runbook? (Omar to confirm)

Next steps (immediate)
- Monday: PM + SRE workshop — finalize SLI definitions for each pilot (agenda attached in Confluence).
- Ravi: populate runbook inventory sheet with current links by EOD Tue.
- Priya: create baseline dashboard queries for p50/p95/p99 + error rate by noon Wed.
- Lena: schedule tabletop slots and invite stakeholders.

Appendix A — quick templates (copy/paste)
- Slack alert template: "[ALERT] {service} {sli} {window} burn-rate {rate}. Runbook: {link} | Oncall: {rotation}"
- Runbook header fields: "Service | Owner | Pager contact | Primary dashboard link | Rollback steps | Escalation steps | Last updated"

Appendix B — quick glossary
- SLI: Service Level Indicator (the metric we measure)
- SLO: Service Level Objective (target on the SLI)
- Error budget: allowed window of failure for the SLO
- Burn rate: speed at which the error budget is being consumed

-- end draft --

(If you're reading this and want to modify the scope: mark changes inline and add a comment with your initials. This doc will be the working artifact until Week 2 sign-offs.)
